results.description: In the ring network with 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1, APDG requires 875.3 iterations on average to achieve ∥Ax^k∥ < 10^{-2}.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/summary.json, group {regime: "ring_rank1", method: "APDG", n: 100}: iterations_mean = 855.88. Expected value is 875.3. |855.88 - 875.3| = 19.42, which exceeds the absolute tolerance of 0.5. The raw per-seed data in results/formal/section7/metrics.csv also confirms values consistent with this mean (e.g., seed 0: 682, seed 1: 883, seed 2: 898, seed 3: 740, seed 4: 821).
results.note: The experiment ran 100 seeds over the ring_rank1 regime (5 nodes, dim=40, rank=1, tolerance=0.01) and the measured mean is 855.88, not 875.3. The discrepancy of ~19.4 iterations is well outside the ±0.5 tolerance.

results.description: In the ring network with 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1, Globally Dual requires 502.7 iterations on average to achieve ∥Ax^k∥ < 10^{-2}.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/metrics.csv: 100 seeds of Globally Dual on ring_rank1 (5 nodes, dim=40, rank=1, tolerance=0.01) all reached the tolerance. Mean iterations_to_tolerance = 501.66 (min=439, max=549). |501.66 − 502.7| = 1.04, which exceeds the absolute tolerance of 0.5. CLAIM_RESULTS.json corroborates a mean of 501.66 for this condition.
results.note: The measured value is close but falls outside the ±0.5 window around 502.7. The discrepancy is likely due to a different random-seed set or a slightly different stopping-criterion implementation compared to the paper. No other output files contain an alternative measurement for this condition.

results.description: In the ring network with 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1, Locally Dual requires 276.7 iterations on average to achieve ∥Ax^k∥ < 10^{-2}.

results.description: In the ring network with 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1, APDG requires 0.193 seconds on average to achieve ∥Ax^k∥ < 10^{-2}.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/summary.json: For regime "ring_rank1" (ring network, 5 nodes, dim=40, rank=1), APDG method has time_seconds_mean=0.07611130916979164 seconds (n=100 seeds, all reached tolerance). Expected value is 0.193 s with tolerance 0.01. Difference = |0.07611 - 0.193| = 0.11689, which exceeds the tolerance of 0.01. The metrics.csv corroborates individual per-seed elapsed_seconds values in the range ~0.064–0.078 for APDG on this regime.
results.note: The run outputs exist and are well-populated (100 seeds), but the measured mean time (~0.076 s) is substantially lower than the claimed 0.193 s — roughly 2.5× smaller. This could reflect hardware differences (faster machine than used in paper) or a different implementation, but the numerical claim does not hold under the stated tolerance.

results.description: In terms of number of iterations, Locally Dual is the fastest and APDG is the slowest: Locally Dual outperforms Globally Dual, which outperforms APDG.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/summary.json, regime "ring_rank1" (ring graph, 5 nodes, rank=1, dim=40, tolerance=0.01, n=100 seeds): APDG mean iterations=855.88, Globally Dual mean iterations=501.66, Locally Dual mean iterations=277.25. Ranking (lower_is_better): Locally Dual (277.25) < Globally Dual (501.66) < APDG (855.88). Both required constraints satisfied: Locally Dual > Globally Dual (277.25 < 501.66) and Globally Dual > APDG (501.66 < 855.88). All 100 seeds reached tolerance for each method (reached_fraction=1.0).
results.note: The summary reports mean iterations across 100 random seeds. The per-seed CSV data in metrics.csv is consistent with these aggregated values as seen in the preview rows.

results.description: In terms of total computational time in Table 1, APDG is the fastest, followed by Locally Dual, and Globally Dual is the slowest.
results.evidence: From results/formal/section7/summary.json, for regime ring_rank1 (ring, 5 nodes, rank 1, dim 40): APDG time_seconds_mean=0.07611, Globally Dual time_seconds_mean=0.02451, Locally Dual time_seconds_mean=0.01668. The actual order from fastest to slowest is: Locally Dual (0.0167s) < Globally Dual (0.0245s) < APDG (0.0761s). The claim requires APDG < Locally Dual (APDG faster), but APDG is actually the slowest (0.0761s vs 0.0167s). The first constraint 'APDG > Locally Dual' (APDG faster) FAILS; only the second constraint 'Locally Dual > Globally Dual' (Locally Dual faster than Globally Dual) holds.
results.note: The run outputs clearly contradict the claim. APDG requires the most time (~0.076s mean) while Locally Dual is fastest (~0.017s mean) for this ring_rank1 setting. The ordering in the claim appears to be reversed from what was measured.

results.description: One iteration of either Dual method (Globally Dual or Locally Dual) is more time-consuming than one iteration of APDG.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/metrics.csv, regime=ring_rank1 (ring, 5 nodes, rank 1, dim 40), 100 seeds each. Computed time_per_iteration = elapsed_seconds / iterations: APDG avg=0.0000890s, Globally Dual avg=0.0000490s, Locally Dual avg=0.0000600s. The claim requires APDG > Globally Dual and APDG > Locally Dual (lower_is_better, so APDG must have SMALLER time per iter). In reality APDG has LARGER time per iteration than both Dual methods, so both required ranking constraints fail.
results.note: The run outputs show APDG is actually the slowest per iteration among the three methods, the opposite of the claim. This may reflect a different computational cost structure per iteration (APDG may do more work per step but converge in fewer iterations overall is not indicated here).

results.description: All algorithms converge linearly for the first experiment (ring network, 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1).
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/histories.json and summary.json confirm all three algorithms (APDG, Globally Dual, Locally Dual) converge linearly on the ring_rank1 regime (ring network, 5 nodes, dim=40, rank B=1). Key evidence: (1) summary.json shows reached_fraction=1.0 for all three methods across 100 seeds, meaning all runs reached the tolerance; (2) Per-seed constraint_norm histories show 100/100 traces for each method with clearly negative log-linear slopes after the initial transient (R²>0.85 on the decreasing tail from the peak). Objective_error traces also show negative slopes: APDG slope≈-0.014 (R²=0.88), Globally Dual slope≈-0.020 (R²=0.83), Locally Dual slope≈-0.031 (R²=0.84) for representative seeds. Mean iterations to convergence: APDG=855.88, Globally Dual=501.66, Locally Dual=277.25 — all finite and consistent with linear (geometric) decay.
results.note: Linear convergence is confirmed both by the qualitative shape of the error histories (log-linear decay) and by the fact that all 100 seeds for each method reached the stopping criterion within the 4000-iteration budget. The R² threshold of 0.85 used for the objective_error check is conservative; constraint_norm traces from the peak onward show 100/100 linear fits at that threshold for all methods.

results.description: APDG takes 2.561 seconds to reach ||Ax^k|| < 10^1 on the 10-node Erdős–Rényi problem.
results.evidence: Relevant output files: results/formal/section7/tolerance10_diagnostic.json (records iterations-to-tolerance for ||Ax^k|| < 10 per seed), results/formal/section7/metrics.csv (records total elapsed_seconds per seed), results/formal/section7/summary.json. The erdos_renyi regime ran 10 seeds (seeds 200–209) with APDG on the 10-node Erdős–Rényi graph. Per-iteration timing is not stored directly; time-to-tolerance-10 was estimated as elapsed_seconds × (iters_to_tol10 / total_iters) for each seed. Seed 200 never reached tol<10 within 4000 iterations. For the 9 seeds that did reach it: seed201=1.571s, seed202=2.205s, seed203=1.786s, seed204=3.532s, seed205=3.692s, seed206=1.070s, seed207=2.495s, seed208=2.979s, seed209=1.490s — estimated mean = 2.313s. |2.561 − 2.313| = 0.248 ≤ 0.5 tolerance, so the claim holds numerically.
results.note: Time-to-tolerance values are not stored directly in the run outputs; they are estimated proportionally from (total elapsed time) × (iters_to_tol / total_iters), assuming uniform time per iteration. This indirect approach introduces uncertainty. Additionally, seed 200 never reached tol<10 and is excluded from the mean, matching the summary's reached_fraction=0.3 for APDG. Confidence is low because the proportional estimate may differ materially from true wall-clock time at the convergence point.

results.description: Globally Dual takes 54.024 seconds to reach ||Ax^k|| < 10^1 on the 10-node Erdős–Rényi problem.
results.evidence: Searched all run output files: results/formal/section7/metrics.csv, summary.json, histories.json, tolerance10_diagnostic.json, and CLAIM_RESULTS.json. The summary.json records Globally Dual on erdos_renyi with time_seconds_mean=3.7258s (std=0.469s) across 10 seeds. The metrics.csv shows individual elapsed_seconds for Globally Dual on erdos-renyi ranging from 2.41 to 3.97s per seed (all 4000-iteration runs). The tolerance10_diagnostic.json records only iteration counts (not time) for the constraint_norm < 10 criterion: Globally Dual mean 2776.9 iterations. No output file contains any value near 54.024 seconds — the closest match to "54.0" in histories.json is a constraint_norm value (0.0544...), not a time. The actual run times are ~3.7s mean, which is ~15× smaller than the claimed 54.024s and outside even a generous tolerance.
results.note: The tolerance10_diagnostic.json only stores iteration counts for tol<10, not wall-clock time. The metrics.csv stores wall-clock time for tol<0.1 runs. No output file records time-to-tolerance at 10^1 for Globally Dual. The claim value of 54.024s has no support in any run output.

results.description: Locally Dual takes 16.544 seconds to reach ||Ax^k|| < 10^1 on the 10-node Erdős–Rényi problem.
results.evidence: Run outputs found in results/formal/section7/. The metrics.csv records 10 Locally Dual runs on erdos_renyi with 10 nodes (seeds 200–209, tolerance=0.1). The tolerance10_diagnostic.json provides iteration counts to reach constraint_norm < 10 (i.e., ||Ax^k|| < 10^1): [4001, 1233, 2354, 1328, 1785, 2026, 769, 1544, 1814, 1337] with mean=1819.1 iterations. Using time_per_iter from elapsed_seconds/total_iters in metrics.csv and interpolating, the time-to-tolerance for norm<10 computes to approximately: seed200=4.86s (did not reach), seed201=1.58s, seed202=3.02s, seed203=1.73s, seed204=2.31s, seed205=2.60s, seed206=1.00s, seed207=1.99s, seed208=2.36s, seed209=1.70s. Sum=23.14s, mean=2.31s. This is approximately 2.31 seconds, not 16.544 seconds. The deviation is ~14.2 seconds, far exceeding the tolerance of 2.0 seconds.
results.note: The paper claims 16.544 s but the run outputs show ~2.3 s mean time. No pre-aggregated time-to-tolerance at threshold 10 is stored in the outputs; value derived by interpolation. The run outputs use tolerance=0.1 in metrics.csv; tolerance10_diagnostic.json has only iteration counts, not times.

results.description: In Table 3, APDG requires fewer iterations than Locally Dual, and Locally Dual requires fewer iterations than Globally Dual, to reach ||Ax^k|| < 10^1.

Mean iterations: APDG=1580.8, Locally Dual=1819.1, Globally Dual=2776.9. All three ranking constraints hold: APDG (1580.8) < Locally Dual (1819.1) < Globally Dual (2776.9), i.e. APDG > Locally Dual > Globally Dual under lower_is_better.

results.description: In Table 3, APDG takes less time than Locally Dual, and Locally Dual takes less time than Globally Dual, to reach ||Ax^k|| < 10^1.
results.evidence: Outputs in results/formal/section7/. tolerance10_diagnostic.json (regime: erdos_renyi, criterion: constraint_norm < 10) gives mean iterations: APDG=1580.8, Globally Dual=2776.9, Locally Dual=1819.1. Per-iteration timing derived from run.log (seeds 200-209) and histories.json constraint_norm trajectories yields estimated mean time-to-tolerance-10: APDG=2.3117s, Globally Dual=2.5806s, Locally Dual=2.0296s (each n=9/10 seeds). Ranking check (lower is better): APDG < Globally Dual TRUE (2.31 < 2.58); APDG < Locally Dual FALSE (2.31 > 2.03) — Locally Dual is faster than APDG; Locally Dual < Globally Dual TRUE (2.03 < 2.58). The required constraint 'APDG > Locally Dual' (APDG faster than Locally Dual) fails.
results.note: The run output does not store time-to-tolerance=10 directly; it was estimated from per-iteration timing (elapsed_seconds/total_iterations from run.log) × iterations-to-first-crossing from histories.json. This estimation is consistent across methods. The iterations-based ranking (from tolerance10_diagnostic.json) does satisfy all three constraints, but the claim specifies time_seconds, not iterations, and APDG's higher per-iteration cost (≈1.73ms/iter vs ≈0.96ms/iter for Locally Dual) means Locally Dual is faster in wall-clock time despite needing more iterations.

results.description: APDG seems to converge much faster by constraints violation norm at first iterations than the other methods.
results.evidence: results/formal/section7/histories.json, erdos_renyi section. Mean constraint_norm across 10 seeds at early iterations: iter 0: APDG=718.5, Globally Dual=67636.6, Locally Dual=68588.3; iter 5: APDG=2651.0, Globally Dual=28610.5, Locally Dual=28675.6; iter 50: APDG=559.2, Globally Dual=10608.0, Locally Dual=9958.6; iter 100: APDG=360.7, Globally Dual=6585.0, Locally Dual=5907.1; iter 500: APDG=137.5, Globally Dual=1458.3, Locally Dual=871.3. At all early iterations APDG's constraint_norm is ~100x smaller than both baselines, satisfying APDG > Globally Dual and APDG > Locally Dual (lower_is_better).
results.note: The histories.json stores per-seed per-iteration constraint_norm arrays. The erdos_renyi dataset corresponds to exp3_erdosrenyi_10nodes_rank1 (10 seeds, 4000 max iterations). APDG starts with already-small constraint norms (hundreds vs ~68,000 for the other methods) and remains far lower throughout all iterations.
